reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation of ALPaCA lies in decoupling meta-learning from online adaptation. It pre-trains a Bayesian prior over kernel matrices (K̄0, Λ0) such that the posterior predictive distribution can be computed efficiently via recursive least squares on a fixed last-layer weight φ. This avoids costly gradient-based updates during inference. The method starts with a multivariate normal prior over kernel matrices, then minimizes expected KL divergence between true and surrogate posteriors across meta-training datasets. At runtime, it uses Woodbury’s identity to compute updated precision Λ_t recursively without refitting the entire model. Predictive mean and variance are derived analytically from this posterior. The key insight is that the feature map φ remains frozen post-meta-training, allowing fast updates while preserving Bayesian semantics. This enables scalable online learning in high-dimensional settings where traditional GP regression becomes intractable due to cubic complexity. In GSI context, this translates to rapid updating of player/team performance beliefs with uncertainty quantification. In GSE, it supports real-time tactical modeling through dynamic belief propagation over state transitions.
